name: Gujarati
signature: Looks like Devanagari with the head-line erased — round tops and no bar running across the top.
combination: A consonant carries an inherent 'a' (ક = ka). A vowel mark (mātrā) replaces that vowel (ક + ી → કી = kī). The virama ્ strips the vowel, and the bare consonant joins the next into a conjunct (ન + ્ + મ → ન્મ). Gujarati is Devanagari's sister, but with one visible difference: it has NO horizontal top line (shirorekhā) — the letters float free, which is why it is sometimes called 'the headless script.'
notes: Used by Gujarati (the language of Gandhi). The initial inventory below covers the greeting/self-introduction/first-verbs vocabulary; it grows toward a complete set. Letterforms mirror Devanagari without the top bar. Stroke orders are the common handwriting convention, not a standard.

components: a joined left curve and lower body
a middle shoulder and small right arch
a separate right stem with a foot
strokeOrder: begin at the upper-left tip and sweep clockwise around the open left curve
continue through the lower body and rise into the middle shoulder
retrace down the shoulder and sweep through the small right arch to its junction
lift once, descend the separate right stem, and curve into its lower-right foot
letters.strokeOrderNote: verified two-stroke teaching-app variant fitted to the bundled printed outline

strokeOrderSource.citation: t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, અ animation, first and second SVG paths
strokeOrderSource.variation: The teaching app animates અ as two ordered pen-down runs. Its first SVG path begins at the upper-left tip, sweeps clockwise around the open left curve, continues through the broad lower body, rises into the middle shoulder, and finishes through the small right arch. The animation then lifts once and its second SVG path descends the separate right stem before curving into the lower-right foot. The app explicitly says that depicted forms and stroke orders can differ by source and should be treated as one variant, not a universal standard. The bundled Noto Sans Gujarati glyph has the same open left curve, joined lower body, middle shoulder, small right arch, and separate full-height right stem, but its printed proportions are broader and its joins more angular than the animated school-hand form. This learner path preserves the source's body-before-right-stem order and one-lift evidence while fitting those movements to the font's ink. Individual handwriting may narrow, round, simplify, or slant either run differently.

letters.notes: The independent vowel a and the inherent-vowel default.

components: a second trailing vertical for ā
strokeOrder: write the joined body of અ
lift and descend અ's right stem
lift again and descend the added trailing ā stem
letters.strokeOrderNote: verified three-stroke teaching-app variant fitted to the bundled printed outline

strokeOrderSource.citation: t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, આ animation, first through third SVG paths
strokeOrderSource.variation: The teaching app animates આ as three ordered pen-down runs. Its first SVG path writes the joined અ body: the upper-left open curve flows clockwise into the broad lower body, rises through the middle shoulder, and finishes through the small right arch. The animation lifts once and its second SVG path descends અ's separate right stem into a lower-right foot. It lifts again and the third SVG path descends the added trailing ā stem into a matching foot. The app explicitly says that depicted forms and stroke orders can differ by source and should be treated as one variant, not a universal standard. The bundled Noto Sans Gujarati glyph preserves the same અ body, first right stem, and extra trailing stem, though its printed body is broader, its joins more angular, and its two stems more widely spaced than the animated school-hand form. This learner path preserves the source's body-before-first-stem-before-trailing-stem order and two-lift evidence while fitting all three runs to the font's ink. Individual handwriting may narrow, round, simplify, slant, or join these parts differently.

strokeOrder: begin in the upper-left and circle the small loop down to the middle crossing
continue through the crossing and sweep clockwise around the broad lower loop
rise along the right side and finish in the upper-right hook without lifting
letters.strokeOrderNote: verified one-stroke teaching-app variant fitted to the bundled printed outline

strokeOrderSource.citation: t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, ઇ animation, first SVG path
strokeOrderSource.variation: The teaching app animates ઇ as one continuous pen-down run in its first SVG path; its remaining path slots are empty. The run begins at the upper-left, sweeps left and down through the small upper loop, returns through the narrow middle crossing, circles the broad lower body, then rises along the right side into the long upper-right hook without lifting. The app explicitly says that depicted forms and stroke orders can differ by source and should be treated as one variant, not a universal standard. The bundled Noto Sans Gujarati glyph preserves the small upper-left loop, narrow middle crossing, broad lower loop, and rising upper-right hook, but its printed lower body is wider and its hook more upright than the animated school-hand form. This learner path preserves the source's upper-loop-to-lower-loop-to-hook order and zero-lift evidence while fitting the motion to the font's ink. Individual handwriting may narrow, round, simplify, retrace, or slant the loops and hook differently.

components: with the hook closed into a loop
a curved body dropping below the line
a stem with a small flag
a vertical spine on the right (no top bar)
a left lobe with an inner curl
letters.notes: The aspirated k — ક said with a puff of breath after it. Gujarati writes aspirated and unaspirated stops as separate letters (ખાવું khāvũ, 'to eat').

components: like દ with an extra inner loop

letters.notes: The retroflex, unaspirated t — the tongue tip curls back to the roof of the mouth, as for ણ, but stops the airflow instead of letting it pass through the nose (રોટલી roṭlī, 'flatbread').

components: a rounded body with a lower hook
letters.notes: The retroflex n — the tongue tip curls back to the roof of the mouth. Middle Indo-Aryan pulled a single n between vowels back to this sound (Sanskrit jānāti → જાણવું jāṇvũ, 'to know').

components: a looped body with an inner curl for aspiration
letters.notes: The retroflex, aspirated dh — curl the tongue back as for ટ and ણ, and add the puff of breath that makes ધ the aspirated partner of દ (મોઢું moḍhũ, 'mouth').

components: a left loop open at the bottom
like વ with an inner bar
a left loop with an inner stroke
a single downward stroke with a small shoulder

letters.notes: The retroflex ḷ, shared with Marathi and the Dravidian south; Hindi lacks it.

marks.attachesAs: a vertical bar to the right of the consonant
a curl placed BEFORE (to the left of) the consonant, though pronounced after
a curl to the right with a tail
a small hook below the consonant
a longer hook below the consonant
the ā bar on the right plus a stroke above
an anusvāra dot above, nasalizing the syllable
a stroke below that removes the inherent 'a' and forms a conjunct with the next consonant
a small hook below (the vocalic r, in Sanskrit loanwords)
